newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy unions say protest still possible over budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy unions say protest still possible over budget.

text.p: Italian unions on Monday moved closer to agreement with Prime Minister Romano Prodi over his 1997 austerity budget but warned that they might still launch protest action if outstanding problems were not clarified.

"A final response to a possible general mobilisation will depend on a new meeting to be held before November 12 which will discuss government fiscal plans," Pietro Larizza, leader of the Uil union, told a news conference.

The leaders of Italy's three main unions, the Cigl, Cisl and Uil, last week raised the spectre of a general strike following an inconclusive meeting with Prodi over budget and labour issues. Fresh talks were held on Monday.
"This time we made progress but the process of clarification is not complete," Larizza told reporters after the meeting.
The unions are particularly anxious about possible cuts to welfare spending and plans to increase the tax burden next year.

They have also demanded reassurances that the centre-left government will not bring forward a review of recent pension reforms and want Prodi to enact a labour pact signed last month which is designed to boost employment.

The 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion) deficit cutting budget is currently passing through the commission stage of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) and is due to go to the full assembly on Wednesday.
A final vote in the chamber is expected by November 17 after which the budget passes to the Senate for further ratification.
The bulk of the budget stems from increased revenues including a one-off "Euro-tax" to help Italy make the grade for membership of Europe's planned single currency.
Union leaders said their worries concerned not only the "Euro-tax" but also planned reform to the fiscal system and property tax as well as job creation and wage settlements. ($1=1,519 lire)
